points: These calls are yours to make. Your opponent is not entitled to make them for you.
You give up the point when the ball in play touches you or anything you wear or carry, except your racket.
You give up the point when you touch the net, or touch your opponent's court, while the ball is in play.
You give up the point when you hit the ball before it crosses the net to your side.
You give up the point when the ball bounces twice on your side, or when your racket hits the ball after it left your hand.
The benefit of the doubt applies here too. If you are not sure the ball bounced twice, you give up the point.

questions.q: Who makes the call when the ball bounces twice on your side?
questions.why: Double bounces, touches and net touches are calls you must make against yourself. Your opponent is not entitled to make them.
questions.ref: Guide section 06, Calls you must make against yourself

questions.q: You run for a drop shot and you are not sure you got it before the second bounce. What do you do?
options: Play on. Doubt goes to the hitter
questions.why: The benefit of the doubt applies here too. If you are not sure whether it bounced twice, you give up the point.
questions.ref: Guide section 06, Calls you must make against yourself

questions.q: During a rally the ball brushes your shirt and then lands in on the other side. What is the call?
options: You lose the point, and you call it yourself
You lose the point only if the opponent saw it
questions.why: You give up the point when the ball in play touches you or anything you are wearing or carrying, except your racket.
questions.ref: Guide section 06, Calls you must make against yourself

questions.q: You hit a volley and your racket touches the net while the ball is still in play. What is the call?
options: Your point, if the ball was already past them
No call unless the net moved
questions.why: You give up the point when you touch the net while the ball is in play.
questions.ref: Guide section 06, Calls you must make against yourself

questions.q: Your opponent says you touched the net. You are sure you did not. Whose call is it?
options: Replay the point when you disagree
The player closest to the net
questions.why: Touching the net is a call you make against yourself. Your opponent is not entitled to make it.
questions.ref: Guide section 06, Calls you must make against yourself

questions.q: Chasing a short ball, your foot lands in your opponent's court while the ball is in play. What is the call?
options: Legal, if you did not get in their way
Legal, if you had already hit the ball
questions.why: You give up the point when you touch your opponent's court with anything while the ball is in play.
questions.ref: Guide section 06, Calls you must make against yourself

questions.q: An easy ball is floating toward the net. You reach over and volley it before it has crossed to your side. What is the call?
options: Legal, if you did not touch the net
questions.why: You give up the point when you hit the ball before it crosses the net to your side.
questions.ref: Guide section 06, Calls you must make against yourself

questions.q: Your racket slips out of your hand, hits the ball, and the ball lands in. What is the call?
options: Good, if the racket stays on your side
questions.why: You give up the point when your racket hits the ball after it left your hand.
questions.ref: Guide section 06, Calls you must make against yourself

questions.q: The ball hits the cap on your head and goes back over the net. What is the call?
options: Play on. A cap is not part of you
Your point, if it lands in
questions.why: You give up the point when the ball in play touches anything you are wearing or carrying, except your racket.
questions.ref: Guide section 06, Calls you must make against yourself
